reading: The National Technical Museum is a Czech institution founded in 1908 that collects, conserves, researches and exhibits the history of technology, industry and science. Its reach extends from a seven-floor Prague building to building heritage at Plasy, railway holdings at Chomutov and postal collections. Its language moves between collections, exhibits, archives, restoration, workshops and research: machines are evidence of how people made and changed the world. The crawl is unusually broad, putting railways, architecture, photography, mining, household technology and the post beside hands-on lessons in springs, statics and printing. A recurring thread is the relationship between an object and its story: what made the railway and what the railway made, a house read through archives, and old processes kept usable through teaching. Accessibility and different ways of learning are also part of the museum’s public mission.

enemies.idea: Interlocking Stalker: a railway signal box on legs throws points under the crew, forcing every escape route onto the track it has reserved.
enemies.why: A railway safety mechanism becomes a readable routing puzzle: interrupt its sequence to cross.

enemies.idea: The Counterfeit Railway lays rails toward every source of useful material, then rewrites the terrain around the line to make the railway seem inevitable.
enemies.why: The exhibition’s two-way question becomes a machine that both builds transport and reshapes what transport serves.

enemies.idea: Spring Collector compresses springs pulled from nearby mechanisms into a bouncing cage; each impact releases another captive coil.
enemies.why: Stored energy makes its attack pattern and the consequences of freeing it physically visible.

enemies.idea: Bearing Mill strips bearings from working doors and wheels, leaving them grinding in place while it rolls effortlessly on its stolen rings.
enemies.why: A small mechanical part creates a tactical contrast between a nimble enemy and a slowing environment.

enemies.idea: Statics Examiner stacks impossible model houses over a corridor and removes one support at a time, testing why the crew’s shelter falls.
enemies.why: The lesson “why does it not fall?” becomes a visible, solvable structural threat.

enemies.idea: Sgraffito Scraper cuts black-and-white layers from walls and folds the peeled designs into sharp decoys.
enemies.why: A decorative technique creates both camouflage and a telltale trail of exposed layers.

enemies.idea: Camera Obscura Hunter projects an inverted view of the room and lunges toward movement in its upside-down image.
enemies.why: The optical reversal gives the crew a learnable way to misdirect it.

enemies.idea: Positive Printer enlarges shadows in a darkroom until they harden into oversized copies that obey the enlarger’s beam.
enemies.why: Changing the light or blocking the exposure gives a fight against copies a hands-on solution.

enemies.idea: Gothic Model Mason assembles miniature pointed arches around intruders, then scales the model up into a full-size stone trap.
enemies.why: A building model becomes a preview of the arena that is about to appear.

enemies.idea: Heat-System Prospector joins obsolete heating systems into a roaming radiator that steals warmth to keep its own mismatched pipes circulating.
enemies.why: Different eras of heating give it conspicuous valves and a route to shut it down.

enemies.idea: House-History Forger pulls old floor plans from a building’s past and makes doors open into rooms that no longer belong there.
enemies.why: Investigating a house’s layered history becomes a navigation puzzle with useful clues in its mismatched rooms.

enemies.idea: Conservation Cradle wraps anything moving in protective supports and tries to immobilize it forever in the name of preservation.
enemies.why: A caring museum function becomes a dangerous capture device that can be persuaded to release its charge.

enemies.idea: Design Cabinet unfolds household lamps, tools and teaching models into an ambush, each object still trying to perform its original job.
enemies.why: Every attack has an ordinary purpose turned inconveniently literal.

enemies.idea: Waterworks Surveyor diverts pipes and gates to classify every corridor as a water structure, flooding routes it cannot catalogue.
enemies.why: The crew can follow the water and reverse the flow rather than simply outfight it.

enemies.idea: Archive Worm eats records of craft and industry, then extrudes metal components based on fragments it has misunderstood.
enemies.why: Partial documents produce surprising, visibly imperfect machines with exploitable missing pieces.

enemies.idea: Departmental Sorter sends objects through a chain of collection, protection and exhibition machines; anything that does not fit gets dismantled for reassignment.
enemies.why: The institution’s connected functions form a conveyor puzzle where interrupting one stage changes the next.

enemies.idea: Horse-Rail Hybrid clips a mechanical horse to a bus chassis and insists both halves follow incompatible transit routes.
enemies.why: Two eras of urban transport pull against one another, giving the crew an opening at junctions.

enemies.idea: Postal Library Moth cross-files technical manuals and postal books, carrying away instructions while leaving convincing but useless substitutes.
enemies.why: A mixed-up reference can send machinery awry, and retrieving the right book repairs the problem.

enemies.idea: Praga Convoy gathers a procession of mismatched historic cars and uses each one to block the next escape route.
enemies.why: A collection of distinct vehicles becomes a moving traffic puzzle without turning a real collector into a monster.

enemies.idea: Electrotechnical Works spins a swarm of shop-floor machines from an imagined factory, converting every recovered component into another electrical hazard.
enemies.why: The factory setting makes the swarm’s manufacture visible and interruptible.

enemies.idea: Photographic Process Leech coats surfaces in light-sensitive layers, recording the crew’s silhouettes and replaying them to draw other machines.
enemies.why: A trace of a past visit can lure enemies or be deliberately planted as a decoy.

enemies.idea: Mine Tourer marks a safe route through a fictional ore-and-coal mine, then moves its markers to herd travelers toward its digging claws.
enemies.why: The unreliable guided route makes observation and marking a return path matter.

allies.idea: The Conservation Bench offers splints and reversible repairs for damaged tools, provided the crew brings back every borrowed support.
allies.why: Preservation becomes practical field support with a small retrieval challenge.

allies.idea: The Railway Signal Tutor shows the crew how the interlocking works through silent movable signals, helping them open a safe route.
allies.why: A surviving interactive teaching device communicates without relying on sound.

allies.idea: The House Reader compares fragments of plans and reveals which sealed doorway belongs to the current building.
allies.why: Research becomes a useful way to resist the swarm’s false architecture.

allies.idea: The Darkroom Instructor develops an image of a hidden mechanism when the crew controls the exposure and protects the paper from light.
allies.why: The ally gives information through a small photographic process the crew performs.

allies.idea: The Library Cart keeps the postal and technical manuals in order and lends a relevant guide when given its title or subject.
allies.why: A quiet research ally rewards remembering and identifying what a machine does.

bosses.idea: The Museum That Makes the World: a vast railway engine drags a factory, building frame and archive behind it, building routes that feed its workshops and workshops that extend its routes.
bosses.why: The museum’s story of technology changing society becomes a feedback loop the crew can break at several linked stages.

bosses.idea: The Perfect Collection: a multi-armed conservation system tries to preserve the whole museum by fixing every machine, room and visitor into an unchanging exhibit. Its protective cradles shield its moving joints.
bosses.why: The institution’s care for objects becomes an overarching conflict between preservation and a living, usable collection.

bosses.idea: The Seven-Floor Demonstrator turns the main building into one giant teaching model, sending loads through beams, rails and electrical machinery while testing the crew’s solutions.
bosses.why: The museum’s stacked breadth becomes a connected encounter where a change on one floor affects another.

events.idea: A model house begins to lean over a passage; a silent teaching mechanism offers three different supports, only some of which keep the load balanced.
events.why: A quick cooperative experiment makes statics tangible.

events.idea: A coil springs out of a dismantled lesson and rolls toward a crack while a swarm scavenger closes in; recovering it restores a nearby mechanism.
events.why: A tiny piece of hardware becomes a chase with a useful reward.

events.idea: In a darkroom, a half-developed photograph shows a route that cannot be seen directly; finish the exposure before a hunter’s light ruins it.
events.why: The crew must manage light and time to get information.

events.idea: An abandoned model of a Gothic arch trembles each time a full-size arch elsewhere is disturbed; the crew can test a repair on the model first.
events.why: A miniature safely previews the consequences of a larger action.

events.idea: Two conflicting plans of the same house lead to different doors. A dated construction detail in the wall reveals which plan fits the present.
events.why: A piece of architectural research resolves a concrete choice.

events.idea: A conservation cradle has secured a useful tool so tightly that pulling it free will damage it; find and release its supports in order.
events.why: Careful handling gives a better outcome than force.

events.idea: An interlocking lever is stuck between two routes while an unmanned rail trolley approaches; resetting the points diverts it into an empty siding.
events.why: A compact railway control problem creates urgency without needing a victim.

events.idea: A rail-laying machine reaches a wall, then starts building a workshop to manufacture a bridge. The crew can interrupt it or use the unfinished span.
events.why: The railway’s effects on its surroundings unfold in real time.

events.idea: A box of postal and technical books has been tipped together; matching a manual to a stalled mechanism earns help from the library cart.
events.why: The joined collections create a small sorting problem with a mechanical payoff.

events.idea: A scavenger is trying to extract bearings from a door that the crew needs. They can distract it, brace the door or recover the rings afterward.
events.why: The same part matters to both the threat and the escape.

events.idea: A mechanical horse and a bus chassis each pull a stranded trolley in a different direction at a junction; uncoupling one frees the route.
events.why: Two eras of transit create a silly but legible mechanical predicament.

events.idea: A set of household lamps flashes in sequence as a design cabinet searches the room. Following the dark gaps lets the crew pass unnoticed.
events.why: A familiar object supplies an observable stealth rhythm.

events.idea: A waterworks model has redirected a trickle into a corridor; turning its miniature gate changes the full-size flow long enough to cross.
events.why: The connection between teaching model and infrastructure invites experimentation.

events.idea: An archive worm has produced an almost-complete mechanism from a torn industrial record. Find the missing diagram fragment to identify its absent part.
events.why: A faulty machine turns archival research into a useful field discovery.

events.idea: A vehicle convoy has blocked itself in a tight turn. Rearranging two cars opens a passage before the rest of the swarm arrives.
events.why: Historic vehicles become pieces in a small spatial puzzle.
